title: Polynomial Features and Overfitting by Hand
learning_objectives: Turn one feature into polynomial features [1, x, x², …]
Fit polynomial models with least squares
Show that training error falls with degree while test error eventually rises
Choose model complexity using held-out data
entry_point: poly_features(x, degree); fit_poly(x, y, degree); predict_poly(coef, x); errors_by_degree(x_tr, y_tr, x_te, y_te, degrees); best_degree(errors)
hints: `np.column_stack([x ** k for k in range(degree + 1)])` builds the feature matrix.
`coef, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(X, y, rcond=None)`; predictions are `poly_features(x, len(coef) - 1) @ coef`.
`min(errors, key=lambda d: (errors[d][1], d))` picks the lowest test error, then the smaller degree.

failure_feedback.advice: Columns must be x**0, x**1, ..., x**degree in that order.
Fit with `np.linalg.lstsq(X, y, rcond=None)` on the polynomial features.
Compute the training error on the training points with the coefficients fitted on them.
Evaluate each model on the test points too; don't refit on them.
Choose by test error (the second value), breaking ties with the smaller degree.
